beur-hagra/1:א: (א) Seif 61: the measure of a kezayit etc. It depends on the view of Tosafot and Rambam regarding eruv. For Rambam ruled in Hilchot Eruvin 1:9 that the measure of an eruv is two meals, which are eighteen dried figs, and they are like six eggs; and this is like RiBBa in Eruvin ch. 2 p. 2 and as the Gemara concludes there "half for the shopkeeper." His proof is because the stam mishnah at the end of Peah is like RiBBa, for there it teaches "one does not give less" etc. from a loaf etc., and it is two meals as explained in the mishnah "eight: one who has food for two meals" etc. Tosafot there ch. 2 s.v. agav ruled like R. Shimon, and they bring proof for their words because the sugya of the Gemara everywhere is like him, for it says "like an egg for impurity" etc. — see there. It is not proof, for Rambam explains what is written everywhere "like an egg for impurity" etc. means without its shell, and do not say literally half of half, as written ch. 3 seif 1 that their measures are not equal to each other. Accordingly it is wondrous what Tosafot explained like R. Shimon would be against the stam of ch. 2 of Peah cited above that follows RiBBa as explained. It appears the stam of Peah is no proof for Rambam; on the contrary, from there is proof for Tosafot who ruled like R. Shimon, for at first glance one could say there, in the mishnah's wording R. Shimon "two handfuls" etc. — why not teach its measure explicitly as a loaf of five eggs and a third? Rather the truth in this appears that the measure of "two handfuls" that R. Shimon says is not the measure of two meals for everyone, but the loaf itself is the d'oraisa measure for an infected house, because it is written "and one who eats in the house" etc., and we require a measure of eating, and half the loaf is the measure of one meal — and this is the "peres" mentioned everywhere, namely a peres of the loaf which altogether is two meals. Only in Eruvin they all intended to be lenient, therefore R. Shimon says two handfuls from it are two meals; likewise Rashi there ch. 2 p. 2 s.v. chatziah even though in the measure etc. — see there. And this is what "chatziah for the infected house" etc. means — why did it not teach its measure explicitly as explained; therefore it says chatziah etc., meaning the essence of its measure is chatziah for the house etc. With this the mishnah's wording in ch. 17 of Kelim is settled, where RiBBa precedes R. Shimon — because here it needed to teach chatziah etc. to reveal that the essence of the loaf's measure is for the infected house, and in Eruvin R. Shimon was lenient, and because of this it used the wording of two handfuls as explained; therefore RiBBa precedes R. Shimon so one should not err and say this chatziah etc. refers to RiBBa alone — if it were taught for RiBBa it would be at the end. (Unlike ch. 17 of Kelim where the mishnah's dispute is not taught there, only incidentally; therefore it did not need to teach again this chatziah etc., and therefore there R. Shimon precedes RiBBa and it is taught with R. Yosi in his dispute.) With this the view of Tur siman 399 who wrote that the measure of two meals is eight eggs is settled — it would be wondrous that they ruled not like whom, and see what is written. But accordingly it is fit: their view that they ruled like R. Yehoshua, who learns from Sifra Parah where he says there "one who eats in the house" ten peres from three kav — he holds like R. Shimon regarding an infected house that half a loaf is one meal, only R. Shimon was lenient for eruv and required only two handfuls as explained; and R. Yehoshua holds that always a peres is half that loaf. And so it appears to them in Tur, since R. Yehoshua states it there stam and we do not hear him in Eruvin to be lenient — if so it is eight eggs as explained. Now at first glance one could say in the sugya of Eruvin there where it says the difficulty of R. Chiya against R. Chiya etc. — what he gave etc. — why does it challenge R. Chiya against R. Chiya? Say the first answer of R. Chiya returns because of the difficulty "still for the master nine" etc., and teach "take from them half" like everywhere; and what does it teach with these two changes that where he gives wood he deducts only a third and where he does not give etc. The matter in this appears that R. Chiya first said the first answer "take from them a third," because the contradiction of these two mishnayot at the end of Peah there was difficult for him, as Yerushalmi challenged there: here you say one does not reduce for the poor at the threshing floor, and there you say one does not reduce for a poor man passing from place to place — meaning since it teaches from a loaf for a pundion, which is half a kav as explained from four se'ah for a sela, for grain not needing baking expense one should give more; and it answers: R. Chiya said take from them a third for going out — meaning what is written from a loaf for a pundion is half a kav less a third, for the shopkeeper profits on baking expense, for since half a kav of wheat is sold for a pundion, when the shopkeeper sells the loaf he deducts his expense; accordingly what is written for grain, half a kav is truly a third more than the measure of a loaf for that pundion — and this is R. Chiya's first answer literally; and that it does not teach "take from them half" is because R. Chiya ruled like R. Shimon and explains the stam of Peah cited above according to R. Shimon, therefore it teaches take from them a third — for accordingly two-thirds of half a kav, the measure of that loaf, are eight eggs, and it is literally like R. Shimon; but afterward it was still difficult for R. Chiya from the baraita that teaches "and close" etc. that is not resolved in the first answer take from them a third, as they challenged in the Gemara there "still for the master nine" etc., and it teaches take from them half — accordingly the Gemara sugya there is fit: at first they wanted to resolve that baraita in the first answer, and because of the Gemara's difficulty "still" etc. it resolved in the second answer take from them half. And it properly challenges these two changes of R. Chiya against each other, and teaches "what he gave" etc. — meaning when he gives to a poor man he need not account for wood expense, therefore they measured there with that loaf for a pundion; and in such a case where the master gives wood he deducts only a third, and where he does not give etc. Accordingly the stam of Peah cited above follows R. Shimon, and R. Chiya holds like him, and so R. Chiya in Yerushalmi — therefore he answered take from them a third as explained to establish that stam like R. Shimon, as written in the Gemara "what he gave" etc.; therefore Tosafot properly ruled like R. Shimon. What Rambam brought as proof from the Gemara's wording there "the Sages — RiBBa" etc., implying halacha is like RiBBa — does not decide against Tosafot, because the stam of Peah is like R. Shimon and halacha follows stam mishnah, as explained. But still uncertain from what is written in Eruvin ch. 2: it teaches that two meals etc., and for RiBBa it is dried figs a third of an egg, and Rambam ruled like him; all the more for Tosafot who ruled like R. Shimon, and a kezayit is less than a dried fig as written in Shabbat seif 1 to exclude dried figs etc.; and in Yoma ch. 1 they said the swallowing organ etc.; and in Keritot 14a they said the swallowing organ does not hold more than two olives, and Magen Avraham and Tosafot there s.v. agav — and because of this Tosafot wrote that for eruv we hold like R. Meir, and in the Gemara too etc. "your father acted like whom — like R. Meir" etc. — see there. R. Meir's measure is unknown, for in the Gemara it says there "two loaves" etc. of the Pappa river. It is possible to say per Tosafot's view R. Meir's and R. Yehoshua's measure cited above is twelve eggs — if so dried figs are two-thirds of an egg, and a kezayit which is less than a dried fig is half an egg, and all is fit. But Rambam's view is still wondrous, for he wrote explicitly that a dried fig is a third of an egg as explained; it appears what Rambam ruled six eggs which are eighteen dried figs as we say in the Gemara there is with shells, and a dried fig for him is a third of an egg with shell; and what is written in Yoma there the swallowing organ etc. more than an egg etc. is without shell, as written there in Eruvin "like it without its shell," and on this they said an olive is half an egg, namely without shell, and the measure of one is only that it is not literally half; therefore he ruled for eruv two meals are six eggs — for accordingly a kezayit is less than a third of an egg as explained; and regarding kezayit measure he wrote it is half an egg, namely as explained; and Shulchan Aruch for eruv wrote like Rambam, and for Passover wrote a kezayit is half an egg — and per what is written, Shulchan Aruch's words here are correct both per Tosafot's view according to R. Meir as explained, and per Rambam's view.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) And one should eat it — as written above siman 475 seif 1.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And regarding vegetables etc. As Tosafot wrote in Yoma 79a s.v. kotevet in the name of Yerushalmi, one must compress its hollow; and as written in ch. 2 of Okatzin regarding onion layers etc., if they have a hollow etc., like sponge cake etc. — see there. And there regarding veal meat etc. But in Menachot 54 we conclude that veal meat that swelled is d'rabbanan, and so Rambam ruled in ch. 4 of Hilchot Avot HaTumah and in ch. 14 of Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot. And at first glance it appears to me that what Ravva said there is a variant reading to avoid difficulty on R. Elazar; but for the conclusion, since R. Elazar's view was accepted in the rejection there, one need not force and say d'rabbanan, and also to say there is no hatara in prohibitions. And in the first chapter of Hametzui it was raised as a question whether there is hatara or not; and although Kesef Mishneh in the name of R' Yitzchak was strained, and Tosafot's difficulty in Menachot there s.v. demei'ikara is also resolved, and also at first glance the sugya in several places that there is hatara in ch. 3 of Taharot regarding gravy etc. — see there. But Rosh and Ra'avad wrote in ch. 3 of Taharot mishnah 4 that there is no hatara, and they adopted the tradents literally; and also Ramban and Rashba in the first chapter of Hametzui strained to resolve Tosafot's difficulty in Menachot cited above and did not reject that halacha — I have no ability to be lenient against them in practice.
chok-yaakov/1:א: (א) That it is like half an egg — so wrote Tosafot Pesachim 108 and in Eruvin ch. Halon — see there; and what Magen Avraham challenged — Tosafot themselves already sensed that difficulty there. And see in Taz ch. 6 of Kelim and at the end of responsum Chut HaShani in the account of calculation, and in Mahariv siman 27, and in Sha'arei Yehuda in his hagahot to Terumat HaDeshen, and see in Beit Hillel on Ohel Moed siman 70.
chok-yaakov/1:ב: (ב) And they should eat together — Tur wrote this law briefly in this siman, and what the Acharonim wrote on this is explained above in its simanim each in its place. And he wrote in pesakim of Mahar"i siman 245 that even if one ate the whole plant, namely one stalk with its leaves, he does not fulfill if there is not a kezayit in it, since the plant is deficient in that he does not eat the roots that are fit to eat — end quote.
peri-megadim/1:ב: (ב) In Tur it is written etc. — see Taz. The laws of the Seder briefly — see Levush; washing the cup — see siman 471 seif 10 and 483, and Beit Meir siman 129 from Shabbat halacha 7 as Magen Avraham wrote Berachot 51a: a cup of blessing — rinse outside and wash inside; and Bach siman 475: on this night even a clean person should rinse and wash — see there; and siman 474: also cups 2 and 4 are included in a cup of blessing and require rinsing; and if they bring him a new cup for cups 2 and 4 he must etc. — see siman 483: on Passover night if he has only one cup that was not dipped, one can say it is permitted to dip in foul water at night for the mitzvah of four cups; and it is possible if he has no water it is permitted to use it thus, for a d'rabbanan positive act pushes aside the prohibition of dipping in glass d'rabbanan, unlike in metal which is d'oraisa — see Yoreh De'ah 120 seif 16; and it is possible this does not apply in our time — see siman 466 — requires study. Our custom is to bring the ke'ara and everything needed before Kiddush at the time he takes the cup for Kiddush; or therefore, or cover with the right hand the bread and afterward uncover the bread — lechem oni; Hagadah on the bread. And he takes a foreleg of a male lamb for a stretched foreleg and remembrance of Pesach if possible, and it should be roasted; and two cooked dishes for the festival offering — even when it falls on Motzei Shabbat take two cooked dishes, only some change and say from Pesachim and sacrifices when it falls on Motzei Shabbat. One need not remove the egg and meat when saying "this bread" as not written in some siddurim. He should intend in the berachah of eating matzah for the korech and afikoman; therefore one should not engage in idle talk until after afikoman — see Shelah. L'chatchila the whole meal is with reclining except Hallel and Hagadah; and in Birkat HaMazon he sits in awe and fear; and b'dieved it suffices with a kezayit of matzah with reclining and with the cups — Magen Avraham in siman 472 ot 7. And he holds all three matzot in his hand when saying HaMotzi, and afterward let the third matzah fall from his hand and bless on the broken and whole upper one for eating matzah, and afterward break a kezayit from each of the whole and broken and eat — see siman 475. And he takes maror a kezayit, for less than kezayit is not eating, and if he cannot — 18; and it is obvious it is forbidden to bless asher kidshanu for eating matzah; and for korech if possible he takes a kezayit — see siman 475 Magen Avraham 8; and if it is very difficult for him, one kezayit for maror suffices; and when he blesses on the first dipping he should also intend for maror and eat in the first dipping less than a kezayit. And if he has only maror — see siman 475 seif 2; nevertheless if he has a vegetable on which he blesses shehakol he may take it and it is b'dieved, and intend also for maror if he said shehakol for that purpose. He should not make Kiddush until it is night, namely tzeit hakokhavim, for one should not make a d'rabbanan safeik l'chatchila — see siman 489. He should hurry to do the whole Seder before chatzot; and b'dieved he eats matzah after chatzot without a berachah — Magen Avraham. Every mitzvah practiced on the first night is practiced also on the second night; a woman does not lead men in Hagadah even on the second night, lest they treat it like the first night in all its stringencies and not treat it lightly. In Tur here it implies immediately after afikoman he should not drink wine — see siman 475 Magen Avraham 1 and see there; and also after removing the table it is between the third and fourth — he should not drink lest he become intoxicated and not say Hallel; the same after afikoman; and some say wine within the meal that does not intoxicate — see siman 479 Taz 2.
